headline: Higher coal and chemical prices lift profit sharply
summary_short: Yankuang Energy's H1 2026 preliminary net profit attributable is guided to roughly ¥4.5B, up about 53% y/y from ~¥3.0B, while Q2 standalone EPS of ¥0.35 fell 11.5% q/q.
summary_long: H1 2026 net profit attributable is preliminarily guided to ~¥4.5B, up ~53% y/y from ~¥3.0B. Company attributes the jump to coal and coal-chemical product prices running at relatively high levels versus the prior-year period, plus investment income from an equity transfer, partially offset by foreign-exchange hedging losses and impairment charges not yet finalized. Separately, Q2 commercial coal sales volume rose 6.29% y/y to 44.61Mt (self-produced coal sales +5.74% y/y to 42.75Mt). Q2 standalone EPS of ¥0.35 fell 11.5% q/q; no y/y comparison is available from shard data.
confidence_notes: No edgarCik; shard sourceLink is a Yahoo fallback. Two WebSearch queries surfaced the company's preliminary H1 2026 profit forecast; the first search's own synthesized answer stated a ~¥7.2B net profit figure but the direct WebFetch of the cited stockstar.com (证券之星, non-aggregator) article explicitly states ~¥4.5B (from ~¥3.0B, +53% y/y) — the fetched primary is used here, and the discrepancy is flagged rather than silently resolved; it may reflect the WebSearch summarizer conflating this with a different entity's figure (a separate CFI.net.cn headline referenced an overseas-listed subsidiary's own H1 2026 results). Coal-volume figures came from the same WebSearch pass, not independently re-fetched. Figures are preliminary/unaudited; the final half-year report was not located within budget. EPS row is the Q2-standalone actual from resolve-earnings-target.mjs's shard KPIs (Yahoo earningsChart) and is not on the same cumulative basis as the H1 profit figure. No sector-specific mining extended metrics apply — the registry's mining set (Cu/Au production, C1, AISC) doesn't cover coal volumes/pricing, so no matching key exists for the disclosed coal-sales figures.

drivers.explanation: Coal and coal-chemical product prices ran at relatively high levels versus the prior-year period, and the company booked investment income from an equity transfer.
Gains were partially offset by foreign-exchange hedging losses and impairment charges the company says are not yet finalized.
